jobs.title: Director, Domain Architect - Global Operational Technology
jobs.description:
Overview

As the Global Operational Technology (OT) Domain Architect, you will define and govern the architecture strategy, standards, reference architectures, and technology roadmaps for PepsiCo's Operational Technology landscape. You will provide architecture leadership across IT/OT convergence, OT architecture governance, OT data & information architecture, OT systems management (OTSM), Industry 4.0 architecture enablement, and OT modernization strategy initiatives supporting PepsiCo's operational environments across Manufacturing, Warehousing, and other operational technology-enabled environments.

You will partner with Engineering, Controls Engineering, Infrastructure, Network Engineering, Compute & Hosting, Cybersecurity, Data & AI, Product, Transformation, and Domain Architecture teams to define integrated architecture strategies, standards, and roadmaps supporting secure, resilient, scalable, and future-ready operational technology ecosystems.

You will serve as the primary architecture leader for the OT domain, ensuring alignment across operational technology, enterprise technology, automation, and emerging Industry 4.0 capabilities through architecture standards, governance frameworks, reference architectures, and technology roadmaps.

Responsibilities

OT Domain Strategy & Architecture:

Define and maintain the Operational Technology domain strategy, standards, reference architectures, principles, and multi-year technology roadmaps.
Establish architecture direction supporting IT/OT convergence, OT modernization, operational resiliency, and future operational technology capabilities.
Evaluate emerging operational technologies in partnership with Technology Strategy, Innovation, and Engineering teams, and define scalable adoption approaches aligned to enterprise standards, business priorities, and long-term technology strategy.
Define architecture enablement strategies supporting Industry 4.0 initiatives including industrial AI, robotics, autonomous operations, advanced sensing, industrial automation, and future operational technologies.

IT/OT Convergence & Governance:

Define architecture frameworks supporting convergence of IT and OT capabilities while maintaining operational safety, reliability, availability, and security requirements.
Establish OT architecture governance frameworks, reference architectures, standards, and decision frameworks supporting global operational environments.
Drive alignment of OT capabilities with enterprise architecture, infrastructure, cybersecurity, data, and operational technology strategies.
Facilitate cross-functional architecture alignment across Engineering, Operations, Infrastructure, Security, Data & AI, and Enterprise Architecture teams.

OT Process Integration Architecture:

Define reference architectures and integration patterns supporting OT lifecycle management, incident management, operational monitoring, observability, and operational support capabilities.
Establish architecture principles that balance enterprise consistency with OT requirements for operational continuity and low-latency environments.
Define reference architectures supporting integrated IT/OT operating models and governance frameworks.
Promote architectural consistency and standardization across operational environments globally.

OT Data Strategy & Information Architecture:

Define OT data architecture principles, information models, classification standards, interoperability requirements, and architecture governance frameworks.
Partner with Data & AI teams to align OT information architecture and data integration requirements with enterprise data standards and platforms.
Define architecture patterns supporting OT data acquisition, integration, visibility, observability, and interoperability across operational technology and enterprise technology environments.
Promote consistency of OT data models, metadata standards, information structures, and data exchange patterns across operational environments.

OT Systems Management & Modernization:

Define architecture strategies supporting OT systems management, lifecycle management, modernization, and technology standardization initiatives.
Establish reference architectures supporting asset discovery, observability, monitoring, operational support, and OT lifecycle capabilities.
Define architecture patterns supporting industrial connectivity, operational intelligence, and future Industry 4.0 initiatives.
Guide technology modernization and rationalization efforts across operational technology environments while maintaining operational continuity.

Vendor & Ecosystem Architecture:

Provide architectural guidance for operational technology vendors, OEMs, automation providers, and industrial technology ecosystems.
Establish architecture standards, reference patterns, and integration approaches supporting interoperability across operational technology platforms and environments.
Support evaluation of technology options, modernization pathways, and platform strategies in collaboration with Engineering, Infrastructure, Security, Procurement, and Technology Strategy teams.
Guide architectural considerations related to vendor dependencies, technology roadmaps, interoperability, supportability, lifecycle considerations, and long-term platform sustainability.

Cross-Functional Architecture Leadership:

Partner with Engineering, Controls Engineering, Infrastructure, Network Engineering, Compute & Hosting, Cybersecurity, Data & AI, Product, Transformation, and Enterprise Architecture teams to define integrated architecture strategies and roadmaps.
Act as the primary architecture integration point across operational technology and enterprise technology domains.
Lead OT architecture reviews and governance activities to ensure alignment with enterprise standards and strategic objectives.
Provide architecture leadership and consultation supporting operational technology initiatives globally.

Compensation & Benefits:

The expected compensation range for this position is between $132,200 - $262,400.
Location, confirmed job-related skills, experience, and education will be considered in setting actual starting salary. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range during the hiring process.
Bonus based on performance and eligibility target payout is 25% of annual salary paid out annually and an additional target payout of 10% of annual salary is paid out over 3 years following the end of the performance period.
Long term incentive equity may be awarded based on eligibility and performance.
Paid time off subject to eligibility, including paid parental leave, vacation, sick, and bereavement.
In addition to salary, PepsiCo offers a comprehensive benefits package to support our employees and their families, subject to elections and eligibility: Medical, Dental, Vision, Disability, Health, and Dependent Care Reimbursement Accounts, Employee Assistance Program (EAP), Insurance (Accident, Group Legal, Life), Defined Contribution Retirement Plan.

The Compensation & Benefit details are subjective to US region and may vary for others based on the location

Qualifications

15+ years of experience in Operational Technology (OT), Industrial Automation, Enterprise Architecture, Engineering Systems, or related technology leadership roles.
Deep understanding of Operational Technology ecosystems supporting Manufacturing, Warehousing, facility automation, material handling, and automated operational environments.
Experience defining architecture strategies, standards, reference architectures, governance frameworks, and multi-year technology roadmaps.
Strong understanding of IT/OT convergence, OT architecture governance, OT systems management (OTSM), OT lifecycle management, operational resiliency, and operational risk management.
Deep understanding of Industry 4.0 technologies and architecture patterns including industrial IoT, industrial AI, automation systems, robotics, autonomous operations, advanced sensing, operational intelligence, and emerging operational technologies.
Experience defining OT data architecture, information models, interoperability standards, metadata standards, and integration architectures across operational and enterprise environments.
Strong understanding of industrial control system environments, industrial communications, plant systems, operational data flows, and operational technology architectures.
Experience developing architecture strategies supporting OT modernization, technology rationalization, lifecycle management, and technology standardization initiatives.
Strong understanding of operational technology vendor ecosystems, OEM environments, modernization approaches, and platform lifecycle considerations.
Proven ability to influence and collaborate across Engineering, Controls Engineering, Infrastructure, Networking, Compute & Hosting, Cybersecurity, Data & AI, Product, and Domain Architecture organizations.
Strong executive communication, stakeholder management, architecture governance, and cross-functional leadership capabilities.
Experience operating effectively within large-scale global, federated, and matrixed organizations.

Differentiating Competencies

IT/OT Convergence Leadership – Connects operational technology and enterprise technology domains through architecture, governance frameworks, standards, and integration patterns.
Operational Technology Domain Expertise – Deep understanding of OT environments, industrial systems, operational constraints, lifecycle management, resiliency requirements, and operational technology architectures.
Industry 4.0 Architecture Leadership – Defines scalable architecture approaches enabling adoption of industrial AI, robotics, automation, autonomous operations, advanced sensing, and emerging operational technologies.
OT Data & Information Architecture – Establishes information architecture, interoperability standards, data integration patterns, and information management frameworks across operational environments.
Enterprise Architecture Mindset – Aligns OT architecture strategies, standards, and roadmaps with enterprise technology direction and long-term business objectives.
Architecture Governance & Standards Leadership – Establishes governance frameworks, decision principles, reference architectures, and standards that drive consistency across operational technology environments.
Cross-Functional Collaboration & Influence – Drives alignment across Engineering, Controls Engineering, Infrastructure, Networking, Compute & Hosting, Cybersecurity, Data & AI, Product, and Domain Architecture teams.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Technology & Security Compliance
jobs.description:
Are you an experienced technology risk and compliance leader ready to make a significant impact on how technology controls protect the integrity of a major enterprise? Join us as Senior Manager, Technology and Security Compliance
and take the lead in strengthening our Sarbanes-Oxley and IT General Controls framework while modernizing how technology risk and compliance are managed across the organization! You’ll shape a controls program that is critical to financial reporting and enterprise risk management, influence key decisions with senior leaders, and drive meaningful improvements across Technology and Cybersecurity. You’ll also build and lead a high-performing team that helps set the standard for technology compliance across the enterprise. This position is in Richmond, VA with a hybrid work schedule. We will consider a remote working option for the ideal applicant.

In this role, you’ll provide both strategic direction and day-to-day leadership across IT systems and security controls, audit readiness, issue remediation, and continuous improvement. You’ll engage closely with Technology, Information Security, Financial Operations, Internal Audit, External Audit, and business stakeholders to strengthen compliance and effectively manage technology risk. We’re looking for a leader with deep SOX and ITGC expertise, a strong understanding of technology risk and security controls, and the executive presence to provide focused program leadership and influence senior stakeholders.

What you will be doing:

Leading the SOX/ITGC controls team in planning, coordinating, and delivering technology control activities across the annual SOX lifecycle, while establishing clear roles, expectations, development plans, and accountability for quality execution.
Overseeing ITGC control design, control ownership alignment, evidence requirements, testing readiness, deficiency evaluation, issue remediation, management responses, and validation of corrective actions.
Establishing consistent standards, procedures, and quality expectations for control documentation, evidence collection, testing support, audit coordination, and remediation governance.
Driving continuous improvement of the SOX/ITGC control environment through simplification, automation, control rationalization, stronger accountability, improved reporting, and risk-based prioritization.
Coordinating SOX and ITGC activities across Technology, Cybersecurity, Finance, Internal Audit, External Audit, application owners, control owners, and business partners to maintain audit readiness and alignment.
Guiding control owners in strengthening control design, clarifying operating expectations, improving evidence quality, identifying root causes, resolving recurring control gaps, and integrating controls with broader technology risk practices.
Translating control risks, audit findings, remediation needs, testing status, control health, and readiness concerns into clear executive communications and decision points while presenting key risk themes to senior leaders and governance forums.

We want you to have:

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Finance, or a related field; Master’s degree preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in SOX compliance, ITGCs, IT audit, technology risk, internal audit, compliance, or related disciplines, including demonstrated experience leading SOX/ITGC activities.
5+ years of leadership experience managing controls teams, audit programs, compliance programs, or multi-functional technology risk initiatives.
Deep knowledge of SOX 404, ITGCs, automated controls, application controls, control dependency mapping, COSO, audit methodology, deficiency assessment, remediation governance, and management response development.
Solid understanding of technology operations and security controls that underpin financial reporting, including IAM, PAM, user access reviews, leading system modifications, infrastructure operations, cloud environments, logging, monitoring, backups, and job scheduling.
Demonstrated ability to establish effective control documentation and evidence standards, coordinate audit and testing activities, manage issue tracking and remediation, improve control execution, and deliver executive-level reporting.
Validated ability to influence senior team members, lead through ambiguity, guide high-performing teams, and communicate technology control risks and sophisticated compliance matters in a clear, executive-ready manner.
CISA, CISSP, CISM, CPA, CIA, or equivalent professional certification required; additional credentials such as CRMA, CGEIT, ISO 27001 Lead Auditor, or other relevant security, audit, risk, or governance certifications preferred.

jobs.title: Vice President, Product & Technology PMO
jobs.description:
About Powerfleet

Powerfleet (Nasdaq: AIOT; JSE: PWR) is a global leader in the artificial intelligence of things (AIoT) software-as-a-service (SaaS) mobile asset industry. With more than 30 years of experience, Powerfleet unifies business operations through the ingestion, harmonization, and integration of data—regardless of source—and delivers actionable insights to help companies meet their strategic objectives around Safety, Compliance, Efficiency and Sustainability. Our people-first culture and relentless innovation empower customers to achieve measurable, sustainable business improvements. Powerfleet serves over 2.6 million subscribers across more than 48,000 customers in 120 countries, with commercial operations across every major continent.

Position Summary

Powerfleet is seeking a Vice President, Product & Technology PMO to lead strategic portfolio management and execution across Product, Engineering, Technology, and enterprise transformation initiatives. This role will establish and drive the operating model, governance, and execution discipline needed to translate Powerfleet’s strategic priorities into measurable business and customer outcomes.

The Vice President, Product & Technology PMO will provide a single, integrated view of major initiatives across the organization, ensuring alignment around priorities, capacity, dependencies, investments, risks, and delivery. Partnering closely with Product, Engineering, Finance, and executive leadership, this role will strengthen portfolio decision-making, improve delivery predictability, and create clear accountability for outcomes.

The ideal candidate is a highly experienced technology and transformation leader who combines strong portfolio management expertise with business and financial acumen and thrives in a fast-paced, global environment.

Key Responsibilities

Portfolio Strategy & Governance

Lead the Product & Technology PMO, including program management, project management, scrum, and delivery resources.
Establish and maintain portfolio governance across Product, Engineering, Technology, and enterprise transformation initiatives.
Develop and manage annual and quarterly planning, prioritization, capacity, and investment processes.
Create a single executive view of strategic initiatives, including milestones, dependencies, risks, investments, resource requirements, and expected outcomes.
Establish clear governance, decision-making, and accountability frameworks to support effective portfolio execution.
Ensure strategic investments remain aligned with organizational priorities and measurable business and customer outcomes.

Program & Delivery Excellence

Partner closely with Product and Engineering leaders to improve roadmap execution, delivery predictability, and time-to-market.
Oversee major technology and enterprise transformation initiatives, ensuring effective planning, execution, and risk management.
Drive cross-functional execution across complex programs involving multiple business functions, technologies, geographies, and stakeholders.
Identify and proactively address organizational, resource, technology, and delivery dependencies that may impact strategic initiatives.
Establish consistent program and portfolio management practices while enabling teams to operate with appropriate flexibility and agility.
Promote a culture of accountability, transparency, and continuous improvement across portfolio execution.

Executive Reporting & Performance Management

Develop executive dashboards and KPIs that provide clear visibility into portfolio health, delivery performance, investment, business value, and customer outcomes.
Provide executive leadership with timely, actionable insights into portfolio progress, risks, dependencies, and decisions required.
Establish mechanisms to measure value realization and business outcomes associated with strategic technology investments.
Improve transparency and consistency in how program performance and portfolio health are communicated across the organization.

Financial & Resource Management

Partner with Finance and executive leadership on portfolio investment decisions, resource allocation, capacity planning, and value realization.
Develop frameworks to evaluate and prioritize investments based on strategic alignment, expected value, resource requirements, and organizational capacity.
Monitor portfolio investments and resource utilization to support informed decision-making and effective allocation of resources.
Balance strategic priorities with available capacity to improve organizational focus and execution.

PMO Transformation & Innovation

Build and continuously evolve a modern, outcome-driven PMO focused on enabling execution rather than traditional project reporting.
Leverage automation, AI-enabled tools, and data-driven insights to improve planning, reporting, forecasting, risk management, and decision-making.
Identify opportunities to simplify processes, reduce administrative burden, and increase the speed and quality of portfolio decisions.
Establish scalable practices and tools that support Powerfleet’s continued growth and transformation.

jobs.description:
Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community? Why settle for just a job when you can land a career? PURPOSE OF THE JOB

Head of the IT Strategy and Transformation Office (STO) leads an integrated enterprise capability that connects strategy, architecture, investment planning, delivery excellence, organizational change, and executive governance. The role brings Enterprise Architecture, Lean Portfolio Management, Agile Delivery (LACE), Organizational Change Management, and Executive Governance together into one accountable operating model. Through this leadership, the Head of IT Strategy & Transformation ensures technology investments are strategically aligned, architecturally sound, appropriately prioritized, delivery-ready, and supported through adoption. The role connects enterprise strategy to execution by enabling informed decisions, focusing resources on the highest-value work, and improving transparency, consistency, and accountability for transformation outcomes.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Leads the Integrated IT Strategy & Transformation Office

Sets the strategic agenda and annual operating plan for the STO, unifying architecture, portfolio, delivery, and governance activity behind one coherent enterprise strategy.
Owns the end-to-end operating model connecting strategy formulation, investment funding, architectural standards, delivery execution, and governance decision rights.
Serves as the single executive point of accountability for whether the organization's technology investments collectively advance its strategic priorities — through the quality of the recommendations, architecture, and delivery readiness the STO brings forward, not through unilateral funding authority.
Represents the STO to the executive team, the Investment Council, and Board-level committees, translating strategic intent into well-formed, architected, and delivery-ready investment recommendations for those bodies to decide.

Enterprise Architecture

Directs the definition of enterprise architecture standards, technology roadmaps, and reference architectures that ensure every investment advances one coherent strategy.
Establishes the architecture governance model — including an Architecture Review Board that evaluates major initiatives for strategic fit, technical risk, and reuse before funding is committed — and delegates day-to-day chairmanship of the Board to the Principal Architect.
Owns the technology rationalization and modernization roadmap, reducing redundant platforms and technical debt over time.

Lean Portfolio Management

Directs enterprise investment planning, aligning funding, capacity, and prioritization with strategic themes and value streams.
Facilitates the Investment Council — a standing committee of executive leaders who hold formal decision-making authority over funding, sequencing, and re-prioritization of major initiatives — by preparing prioritized investment recommendations, portfolio trade-off analysis, and capacity/value data for the committee's decisions. The Head of IT Strategy & Transformation does not hold personal or unilateral funding decision rights.
Owns portfolio-level value realization: tracking benefits, cost, and capacity against plan, and reallocating investment as strategic priorities shift.

Agile Delivery (LACE)

Builds and matures enterprise delivery capability through the Lean-Agile Center of Excellence — coaching, engineering practices, and operating model maturity across delivery teams.
Scope note: LACE owns the ways of working and delivery-team practices used to build initiatives; it does not own business-side adoption of the resulting process or operational changes — that responsibility sits with Organizational Change Management, below.
Sets delivery standards and operating cadences (e.g., Program Increment planning, Scrum of Scrums) that give the portfolio a predictable, transparent delivery rhythm.
Establishes delivery KPIs (predictability, flow, quality, cycle time) and drives continuous improvement across delivery teams.

Executive Governance

Personally designs, chairs, and runs the decision forums and escalation paths that connect strategy, investment, architecture, and execution — including cadence, membership, and decision rights for each forum. This is not delegated to a direct-report manager; the Head of IT Strategy & Transformation is the accountable owner of governance.
Ensures every major decision (funding, architecture exception, delivery risk) is made in the right forum, by the right owner, with the right information, and personally facilitates the highest-stakes / executive-level sessions.
Publishes and maintains a governance operating calendar and RACI so accountability is explicit at every level of the model; may be supported by governance/PMO analysts for administration and reporting, but retains direct ownership of the function.
Serves as the escalation point of last resort within the STO for unresolved cross-discipline conflicts (e.g., architecture vs. delivery timeline, portfolio priority disputes).

Organizational Change Management

Owns enterprise-level change leadership for the operational and process-related impacts of major initiatives on the business — how work gets done, roles change, and processes are re-designed — as distinct from LACE's focus on delivery-team ways of working.

Directs the Manager, Organizational Change Management to build and run a repeatable OCM methodology (stakeholder analysis, change impact assessment, communication planning, training, and adoption measurement) applied consistently across major initiatives.

Ensures every initiative entering the portfolio carries a change-readiness assessment and a named change plan before it is funded, closing a common gap where technical delivery outpaces organizational readiness.

Personally sponsors change management for the STO's own operating model — leading the organization through the shift to a unified strategy, architecture, portfolio, and governance function, including communication, training, and adoption of new decision rights and cadences.

Partners with HR, Communications, and business-unit leaders to align change plans with broader organizational initiatives and to manage change fatigue across concurrent transformations.

Establishes adoption and sentiment metrics (e.g., stakeholder readiness scores, training completion, adoption rates) and reviews them alongside delivery and portfolio KPIs so change outcomes are tracked with the same rigor as cost and schedule.

Team Leadership and Development

Provides strategic, tactical, and day-to-day direction to the architecture, portfolio, delivery, and change management leads who report into the STO.

Builds a cohesive leadership team across historically separate disciplines, establishing shared metrics, cadence, and a common operating language — while personally modeling the governance standard the team is held to, since the Head of IT Strategy & Transformation owns that discipline directly.

Owns hiring, performance management, coaching, and development planning for direct reports; holds them accountable for the same standard across their functions.

Manages the STO's budget, staffing, and vendor/consulting resources, and ensures adherence to company policy and compliance requirements.

Acts as an escalation point and thought partner for the organization on complex, cross-functional strategy, architecture, portfolio, or delivery problems.

Supervisory Responsibilities

Directly supervises the leaders of Enterprise Architecture, Lean Portfolio Management, Agile Delivery (LACE), and Organizational Change Management, and carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with company policies and applicable laws. Executive Governance is run by the Head of IT Strategy & Transformation directly and has no dedicated manager. Supervisory responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, and training team members; planning, assigning, and directing work; conducting performance and salary reviews; rewarding and disciplining staff; addressing complaints and resolving problems; coaching, mentoring, and developing direct reports and their teams; creating and monitoring development plans; setting performance expectations and goals; forecasting staffing needs across the STO; and enforcing department policies and procedures.

Education And Experience

Bachelor's degree from a four-year college or university required, in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Administration, or a related field; Master's degree (MBA or equivalent) preferred.
Minimum 12 years of progressive experience across enterprise architecture, portfolio management, agile delivery, or IT/business strategy.
Minimum 7 years in a leadership role managing multidisciplinary teams and/or a Strategy, Transformation, PMO, or Enterprise Architecture function.
Demonstrated track record building or leading a Lean Portfolio Management model, Agile Center of Excellence, or comparable transformation function.

CERTIFICATES AND LICENSES

SAFe Program Consultant (SPC) or SAFe Agilist required; SAFe Lean Portfolio Management (LPM) certification preferred. TOGAF or equivalent enterprise architecture certification preferred. Prosci Change Management Certification or equivalent OCM credential preferred. PMP, PgMP, or ITIL certification a plus.

Knowledge And Skills

Deep working knowledge of enterprise architecture frameworks, Lean Portfolio Management, SAFe or comparable scaled-agile operating models, and executive governance design.
Proven ability to translate enterprise strategy into a funded, architected, and delivery-ready portfolio of initiatives.
Skilled at designing governance forums, decision rights, and operating cadences that hold a large organization accountable without adding bureaucracy.

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

About the Team

Talent Acquisition & Management at ServiceNow is building the systems and strategy behind AI-native hiring at scale. As we bring our new Avature platform online this December, we need someone to own what happens next: the day-to-day design, operations, and TA Tech vendor relationships that keep our foundational TA systems running well and running smart.

About The Role

We're looking for a true subject-matter expert who can bridge deep TA process knowledge with strong systems and vendor management skills, someone who makes sure the technology recruiters rely on every day just works and keeps getting better. You'll work in constant partnership with Product and DT, and be the voice of TA in those rooms: someone who understands how recruiters actually source, screen, and move candidates, and who can translate a system change into what it means for hiring velocity and candidate experience. You'll own the future strategy design and day-to-day operations of Avature and our other foundational TA&M systems and program partnerships as we bring them online, acting as the translator between our business strategy and the systems that power it.

What You'll Own

Avature Post-Implementation: full ownership of platform optimization, adoption, and operational excellence following our December go-live, including vendor relationship management and quarterly business reviews.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: serving as the primary liaison between TA, the Project Madagascar program team, and People Product & DT, translating technical requirements into what they mean for the TA practitioner.
TA Technology Stack Optimization: governance and design for our foundational TA systems (Avature, LinkedIn, HackerRank, Findem and more as we bring new tools online), ensuring interoperability and long-term reliability, with Customer Zero and Now on Now top of mind, always looking for where we can lean further into our own ServiceNow platform as part of our broader strategy heading into next year.
Pre-Go-Live Implementation Readiness: partnering with the Project Madagascar change team on training, documentation, cutover planning, and day-one support.
Vendor Relationship Management: receiving vendor handoffs from our Innovation team and owning ongoing partnership, SLA accountability, contract renewals, and optimization conversations.
Operational Metrics & Governance: establishing and tracking system health, adoption, and performance KPIs that feed directly into our roadmap decisions.

Qualifications

What You'll Bring

Background in TA technology, operations, and strategy; Avature experience is strongly preferred.
Prior experience as a recruiter or sourcing practitioner is a big plus; it's what lets you speak the language of the team you're serving.
A track record of owning vendor relationships and driving system adoption at scale.
Expert-level collaboration skills and cross-functional experience; there are strong relationships between our TA CoE, Product and DT teams and connectedness while working as a team is a critical piece of this role.
The judgment to operate independently while staying tightly aligned with TA strategy.

new_jobs.title: Head of IT Strategy and Transformation
new_jobs.description:
Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community? Why settle for just a job when you can land a career? At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our journey as we strive to transform the insurance carrier space. We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.

Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for the twelfth consecutive year in a row and for the 20th time overall as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!

PURPOSE OF THE JOB

Head of the IT Strategy and Transformation Office (STO) leads an integrated enterprise capability that connects strategy, architecture, investment planning, delivery excellence, organizational change, and executive governance. The role brings Enterprise Architecture, Lean Portfolio Management, Agile Delivery (LACE), Organizational Change Management, and Executive Governance together into one accountable operating model. Through this leadership, the Head of IT Strategy & Transformation ensures technology investments are strategically aligned, architecturally sound, appropriately prioritized, delivery-ready, and supported through adoption. The role connects enterprise strategy to execution by enabling informed decisions, focusing resources on the highest-value work, and improving transparency, consistency, and accountability for transformation outcomes.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Leads the Integrated IT Strategy & Transformation Office

Sets the strategic agenda and annual operating plan for the STO, unifying architecture, portfolio, delivery, and governance activity behind one coherent enterprise strategy.
Owns the end-to-end operating model connecting strategy formulation, investment funding, architectural standards, delivery execution, and governance decision rights.
Serves as the single executive point of accountability for whether the organization's technology investments collectively advance its strategic priorities — through the quality of the recommendations, architecture, and delivery readiness the STO brings forward, not through unilateral funding authority.
Represents the STO to the executive team, the Investment Council, and Board-level committees, translating strategic intent into well-formed, architected, and delivery-ready investment recommendations for those bodies to decide.

Enterprise Architecture

Directs the definition of enterprise architecture standards, technology roadmaps, and reference architectures that ensure every investment advances one coherent strategy.
Establishes the architecture governance model — including an Architecture Review Board that evaluates major initiatives for strategic fit, technical risk, and reuse before funding is committed — and delegates day-to-day chairmanship of the Board to the Principal Architect.
Owns the technology rationalization and modernization roadmap, reducing redundant platforms and technical debt over time.

Lean Portfolio Management

Directs enterprise investment planning, aligning funding, capacity, and prioritization with strategic themes and value streams.
Facilitates the Investment Council — a standing committee of executive leaders who hold formal decision-making authority over funding, sequencing, and re-prioritization of major initiatives — by preparing prioritized investment recommendations, portfolio trade-off analysis, and capacity/value data for the committee's decisions. The Head of IT Strategy & Transformation does not hold personal or unilateral funding decision rights.
Owns portfolio-level value realization: tracking benefits, cost, and capacity against plan, and reallocating investment as strategic priorities shift.

Agile Delivery (LACE)

Builds and matures enterprise delivery capability through the Lean-Agile Center of Excellence — coaching, engineering practices, and operating model maturity across delivery teams.
Scope note: LACE owns the ways of working and delivery-team practices used to build initiatives; it does not own business-side adoption of the resulting process or operational changes — that responsibility sits with Organizational Change Management, below.
Sets delivery standards and operating cadences (e.g., Program Increment planning, Scrum of Scrums) that give the portfolio a predictable, transparent delivery rhythm.
Establishes delivery KPIs (predictability, flow, quality, cycle time) and drives continuous improvement across delivery teams.

Executive Governance

Personally designs, chairs, and runs the decision forums and escalation paths that connect strategy, investment, architecture, and execution — including cadence, membership, and decision rights for each forum. This is not delegated to a direct-report manager; the Head of IT Strategy & Transformation is the accountable owner of governance.
Ensures every major decision (funding, architecture exception, delivery risk) is made in the right forum, by the right owner, with the right information, and personally facilitates the highest-stakes / executive-level sessions.
Publishes and maintains a governance operating calendar and RACI so accountability is explicit at every level of the model; may be supported by governance/PMO analysts for administration and reporting, but retains direct ownership of the function.
Serves as the escalation point of last resort within the STO for unresolved cross-discipline conflicts (e.g., architecture vs. delivery timeline, portfolio priority disputes).

Organizational Change Management

Owns enterprise-level change leadership for the operational and process-related impacts of major initiatives on the business — how work gets done, roles change, and processes are re-designed — as distinct from LACE's focus on delivery-team ways of working.

Directs the Manager, Organizational Change Management to build and run a repeatable OCM methodology (stakeholder analysis, change impact assessment, communication planning, training, and adoption measurement) applied consistently across major initiatives.

Ensures every initiative entering the portfolio carries a change-readiness assessment and a named change plan before it is funded, closing a common gap where technical delivery outpaces organizational readiness.

Personally sponsors change management for the STO's own operating model — leading the organization through the shift to a unified strategy, architecture, portfolio, and governance function, including communication, training, and adoption of new decision rights and cadences.

Partners with HR, Communications, and business-unit leaders to align change plans with broader organizational initiatives and to manage change fatigue across concurrent transformations.

Establishes adoption and sentiment metrics (e.g., stakeholder readiness scores, training completion, adoption rates) and reviews them alongside delivery and portfolio KPIs so change outcomes are tracked with the same rigor as cost and schedule.

Team Leadership and Development

Provides strategic, tactical, and day-to-day direction to the architecture, portfolio, delivery, and change management leads who report into the STO.

Builds a cohesive leadership team across historically separate disciplines, establishing shared metrics, cadence, and a common operating language — while personally modeling the governance standard the team is held to, since the Head of IT Strategy & Transformation owns that discipline directly.

Owns hiring, performance management, coaching, and development planning for direct reports; holds them accountable for the same standard across their functions.

Manages the STO's budget, staffing, and vendor/consulting resources, and ensures adherence to company policy and compliance requirements.

Acts as an escalation point and thought partner for the organization on complex, cross-functional strategy, architecture, portfolio, or delivery problems.

Supervisory Responsibilities

Directly supervises the leaders of Enterprise Architecture, Lean Portfolio Management, Agile Delivery (LACE), and Organizational Change Management, and carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with company policies and applicable laws. Executive Governance is run by the Head of IT Strategy & Transformation directly and has no dedicated manager. Supervisory responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, and training team members; planning, assigning, and directing work; conducting performance and salary reviews; rewarding and disciplining staff; addressing complaints and resolving problems; coaching, mentoring, and developing direct reports and their teams; creating and monitoring development plans; setting performance expectations and goals; forecasting staffing needs across the STO; and enforcing department policies and procedures.

Education And Experience

Bachelor's degree from a four-year college or university required, in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Administration, or a related field; Master's degree (MBA or equivalent) preferred.
Minimum 12 years of progressive experience across enterprise architecture, portfolio management, agile delivery, or IT/business strategy.
Minimum 7 years in a leadership role managing multidisciplinary teams and/or a Strategy, Transformation, PMO, or Enterprise Architecture function.
Demonstrated track record building or leading a Lean Portfolio Management model, Agile Center of Excellence, or comparable transformation function.

CERTIFICATES AND LICENSES

SAFe Program Consultant (SPC) or SAFe Agilist required; SAFe Lean Portfolio Management (LPM) certification preferred. TOGAF or equivalent enterprise architecture certification preferred. Prosci Change Management Certification or equivalent OCM credential preferred. PMP, PgMP, or ITIL certification a plus.

Knowledge And Skills

Deep working knowledge of enterprise architecture frameworks, Lean Portfolio Management, SAFe or comparable scaled-agile operating models, and executive governance design.
Proven ability to translate enterprise strategy into a funded, architected, and delivery-ready portfolio of initiatives.
Skilled at designing governance forums, decision rights, and operating cadences that hold a large organization accountable without adding bureaucracy.

new_jobs.description:
Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

About the Team

Talent Acquisition & Management at ServiceNow is building the systems and strategy behind AI-native hiring at scale. As we bring our new Avature platform online this December, we need someone to own what happens next: the day-to-day design, operations, and TA Tech vendor relationships that keep our foundational TA systems running well and running smart.

About The Role

We're looking for a true subject-matter expert who can bridge deep TA process knowledge with strong systems and vendor management skills, someone who makes sure the technology recruiters rely on every day just works and keeps getting better. You'll work in constant partnership with Product and DT, and be the voice of TA in those rooms: someone who understands how recruiters actually source, screen, and move candidates, and who can translate a system change into what it means for hiring velocity and candidate experience. You'll own the future strategy design and day-to-day operations of Avature and our other foundational TA&M systems and program partnerships as we bring them online, acting as the translator between our business strategy and the systems that power it.
